note: Which land mass a place stands on, for a journey over the ground: between two of them a vehicle needs a ship, a shuttle train or a flight. Filed by country, with boxes (land mass, country, south, north, west, east) for islands that belong to a country filed elsewhere. Made for this skill from the map, as a warning and not an authority: a country of many islands counts as one piece unless a box says otherwise, small islands are not listed, and nothing here knows of a closed border or a road that is shut. The live map decides.

sources.LeShuttle: leshuttle.com, read 2026-11-12: cars ride a shuttle train through the Channel Tunnel between Folkestone and Calais, 35 minutes; arrive at the terminal at least 1 hour before departure ('On the day'). The Dover to Calais ferry takes 90 minutes at its quickest ('Driving to Calais')
sources.Wikipedia, Darien Gap: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darien_Gap, read 2026-11-12: the gap interrupts the Pan-American Highway, which breaks at Yaviza in Panama and resumes at Turbo in Colombia, roughly 106 km away

great-britain|mainland.text: Great Britain has no road to the mainland. A car crosses on the shuttle train through the Channel Tunnel, between Folkestone and Calais, or on a ferry
great-britain|mainland.adds: 35 min on board, after arriving 1 h before departure as the operator asks. The quickest ferry is 90 min on board, and a queue at the terminal or the port is not counted [LeShuttle]

north-america|south-america.text: North and South America are joined by land but not by road: the Pan-American Highway breaks at the Darien gap, roughly 106 km between Yaviza in Panama and Turbo in Colombia [Wikipedia, Darien Gap]. A vehicle goes round by sea
